text:
claire.nguyen: Hey team, escalation from EU customer: spikes of 300-700ms plus intermittent 401s after a recent deploy. They say their requests include X-Client-Region: eu-west1 but our logs show requests hitting us-west1 clusters. Ticket #C-3821. Repro steps below.

support-bot: Created internal ticket S-1987 and linked C-3821.

claire.nguyen: Repro command the customer ran: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Host: api.redwood-inference.com" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west1" "https://gateway.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
They also included client_request_id header: 45f2a1.

samir.khan: I can reproduce a latency jump and occasional 401 when I set X-Client-Region=eu-west1 but omit the Authorization header then retry with token. Logs show route matched default_cluster -> us-west1.

matt.devon: looking at the envoy logs: when route fallback occurs we see header rewrite that strips X-Client-Region on upstream redirect. Example log excerpt: 
```
[envoy][2025-01-11T14:22:03Z] route matched: cluster=default_cluster_us-west1; header_rewrite: set_host=us-west1.internal
upstream_headers: -x-client-region (removed)
```

luisa.ops: That explains the auth 401: auth service validates region header for token audience. If header is lost, token looks mismatched -> 401. Also cross-region -> latency.

samir.khan: Quick repro script I used: 
```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Host: api.redwood-inference.com" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" https://gateway.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate; sleep 0.5;
done
```
I saw first call 200 (eu), next call fell back to 401+1.1s (us).

matt.devon: Root cause hypothesis: L7 route matcher has a fallback path that rewrites host to default and inadvertently drops region header when doing a cluster rewrite. The config has `host_rewrite` + `upgrade_configs` that trigger on certain upstream responses.

luisa.ops: Proposed immediate mitigation: enable `preserve_external_headers: true` on the edge listener for the eu region, and disable `enable_cross_region_fallback` flag to avoid silent reroutes while we fix config. Rolling a patch to canary eu-edge now.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary deploy started for eu-edge config change (canary-id: canary-909). Healthchecks running.

matt.devon: I've opened PR #4521 with the route change and a unit test to ensure x-client-region is preserved across host_rewrite. Also added a tracing span so we can see header propagation.

samir.khan: Verified PR on local envoy with our repro script — header preserved, no 401, latency stable ~90ms in eu.

claire.nguyen: Messaging update to customer: "We're seeing an Envoy route fallback that rewrites host and drops region header, causing cross-region routing and token mismatch. We're rolling a canary fix to preserve region headers and disable automatic cross-region fallback. Will update once canary is healthy." :white_check_mark:

luisa.ops: Monitoring note — added metric `edge.header_preserve.failures` and alert if >5/min. Also created dashboard showing region drift counts by client_request_id.

matt.devon: Follow-up: long-term fix tracked in ENG-CR-178: remove implicit fallback cluster for region hints and add explicit route tiers per region + test matrix for header preservation.

claire.nguyen: Customer updated: they confirmed improved latency after our change and fewer 401s. Keeping ticket open until full rollout. Thanks everyone. :pray:
